accepted.title: Power-biased one-sided transposition cutoff on generalized symmetric groups
accepted.text: For each fixed integer r≥1, let G_{r,n}=(Z/r)^n⋊S_n and start at the identity. Write ξ_j for adding one unit of colour at position j. At each step independently choose j with probability j^α/N_α(n), i uniformly from {1,…,j}, and k uniformly from Z/r. For i<j multiply by ξ_i^k ξ_j^k(ij); for i=j multiply by ξ_j^k, so the coincident position is coloured once. For a fixed real α, put N_α(n)=Σ_{j=1}^n j^α and t_{n,α}=N_α(n)/n^α when α≤1, and t_{n,α}=N_α(n)/N_{α−1}(n) when α≥1 (the formulas agree at α=1). Let μ_{n,t} be the law after t steps and π_{r,n} the uniform law; define d_n^{TV}(t)=½Σ_{σ∈G_{r,n}}|μ_{n,t}(σ)−π_{r,n}(σ)|. For a distance d_n(t) from the uniform distribution, cutoff at a_n means that for each ε∈(0,1), d_n(⌊(1−ε)a_n⌋)→1 and d_n(⌈(1+ε)a_n⌉)→0 as n→∞. For every fixed r≥1 and fixed α∈R, does this shuffle have total variation cutoff at a_n=t_{n,α}log n?

accepted.scope_review: Read held PDF definitions 3.6.1, 4.4.1 and 4.5.1, source time convention in Theorem 3.6.6, and the full statements and adjacent proofs of Conjectures 3.7.9, 4.4.4, 4.5.8. α is fixed independently of n, and the weight function is position-only. The shuffle starts at the identity; uniform is stationary. The positive-α separation target differs from total variation. The hyperoctahedral and all-fixed-r total variation questions are related as special case/generalization, not equivalent full scopes. The source uses the same colour k at both distinct positions, and one update for coincident positions as its Thm 4.5.9 proof states. Do not replace k at the second position by −k; that would agree for r=2 but give a different chain for r>2. r is fixed, not allowed to grow with n.
accepted.duplicate_review: No numbered full target found. The r=1 power-bias theorem and r=2 α≤0 theorem are known; r=2 all-α limsup bound is a related recommendation, not identical to this full all-r ratio-cutoff target.
accepted.literature_finding: Deng–Tan February 2024 proves unbiased fixed-r cutoff and explicitly leaves power-biased cutoff conjectural; its introduction has swapped labels for the two spectral conjectures, so exact source labels control this packet. No exact later resolution was found in current primary retrieval.
